settings.title: Bones & Teeth
settings.tagline: The foundation of your body's structure
settings.text: Your bones provide structural support, protect vital organs and work together with muscles to enable movement. Your teeth rely on mineralised structures to maintain their strength and function. Maintaining normal bone and dental health involves several nutrients, including calcium, vitamin D, vitamin K, magnesium, phosphorus and zinc.
Selected ingredients in HLTHX are relevant to bone and teeth health.
settings.footnote: *Compound ingredient weights, not elemental mineral quantities.

settings.name: Vitamin D3
settings.text: Helps the body absorb and utilise calcium and contributes to the maintenance of normal bones and teeth.

settings.name: Vitamin K2 MK-7
settings.text: Vitamin K contributes to normal bone maintenance. MK-7 is a form of vitamin K2 studied in relation to bone metabolism.

settings.name: Calcium
settings.text: Calcium is a major structural mineral in bones and teeth and is needed for their maintenance.

settings.name: Magnesium
settings.text: Magnesium contributes to the maintenance of normal bones and plays a role in normal muscle and nerve function.

settings.name: Phosphorus
settings.text: Phosphorus contributes to the maintenance of normal bones and teeth and is a component of the body's mineral structures.

settings.name: Zinc
settings.text: Zinc contributes to the maintenance of normal bones and plays a role in normal protein synthesis.

settings.title: Effect of calcium and vitamin D supplementation on bone mineral density in women aged 65–71 years: a 3-year randomized population-based trial (OSTPRE-FPS).
settings.findings: In the intention-to-treat analysis, total-body bone mineral density increased by 0.84% in the supplementation group compared with 0.19% in the control group. The difference was statistically significant. However, differences at several individual skeletal sites, including the lumbar spine and femoral neck, were not statistically significant.
settings.meaning:
This trial provides human research evidence on the relationship between calcium and vitamin D supplementation and bone mineral density in older women. HLTHX contains vitamin D3 at 600 IU per sachet, compared with 800 IU in the study.

The study supports the scientific relevance of calcium and vitamin D to bone health. It does not prove that HLTHX produces the same results.
